question: What are the three distinct phases that make up peri-operative nursing care?
explanation: Peri-operative care is formally divided into the pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative phases to cover the entire surgical experience. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why must a peri-operative nurse understand all three phases of surgery?

options.A: To replace the surgeon during emergencies in the theatre
options.B: To manage the hospital billing department effectively
options.C: To anticipate complications and coordinate seamless patient care
options.D: To prescribe appropriate medications without a doctor

explanation: Knowing the whole surgical continuum helps the nurse foresee risks and maintain continuity of care from ward to theatre and back. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h1)

question: When does the pre-operative phase of nursing care officially end?

options.A: When the surgeon finishes the primary incision
options.B: When the patient is transferred to the operating theatre
options.C: When the patient wakes up in the recovery room
options.D: When the patient is discharged home from the ward

explanation: The pre-operative phase starts with the decision for surgery and ends the moment the patient enters the operating theatre. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for elective hernia repair admits to eating a meal an hour ago. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Proceed with the surgery since a hernia repair is minor
options.B: Administer a strong laxative to clear the stomach contents
options.C: Inform the surgical team immediately to delay the procedure
options.D: Ask the patient to drink plenty of water to dilute the meal

explanation: Fasting status is critical to prevent aspiration during anesthesia, so the surgical team must be notified to reschedule. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which intra-operative nurse works within the sterile field handling surgical instruments?
explanation: The scrub nurse is part of the sterile team who directly assists the surgeon by handling instruments at the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary responsibility of the circulating nurse during an operation?

options.A: Closing the subcutaneous tissue and skin layers
options.B: Performing the primary surgical incision on the patient
options.C: Managing the non-sterile environment and patient safety

explanation: The circulating nurse stays outside the sterile field to coordinate room activities, monitor safety, and keep accurate records. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the immediate priority for a nurse receiving a patient in the recovery room?

options.A: Maintaining a patent airway and supporting breathing
options.B: Offering the patient a warm drink of water
options.C: Changing the primary surgical wound dressing
options.D: Discharging the patient back to the home environment

explanation: Airway management is always the first priority in the PACU due to the lingering effects of anesthesia. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h4)

question: A post-operative patient has a sudden drop in blood pressure and a rapid, weak pulse. What complication should the nurse suspect?
explanation: Hypotension and tachycardia are classic clinical signs of fluid volume loss, which often points to internal bleeding after surgery. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which tool is universally used by surgical teams to verify patient safety before an incision?
explanation: The WHO checklist is a standard communication and safety tool used to prevent errors during surgery. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why is the nurse considered a patient advocate during the intra-operative phase?

options.A: The nurse has legal authority to overrule the lead surgeon
options.B: The patient is unconscious and unable to speak for themselves
options.C: The hospital management requires the nurse to defend the budget
options.D: The family expects the nurse to perform the surgery instead

explanation: Because patients under anesthesia cannot voice their needs, the nurse protects their safety, rights, and well-being. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the primary legal purpose of nursing documentation in the operating theatre?

options.A: To calculate the monthly salary of the surgical staff
options.B: To serve as an official record of the care provided
options.C: To advertise hospital success rates to the public
options.D: To replace verbal handovers entirely during shifts

explanation: Medical records are legal documents that prove what assessments, interventions, and nursing actions were actually performed. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which practice should a nurse avoid when documenting peri-operative care?

options.A: Documenting patient responses to pain medication accurately
options.B: Recording care hours after the shift has ended from memory
options.C: Writing clear, objective statements about wound conditions
options.D: Signing and dating every single nursing entry promptly

explanation: Delayed documentation from memory invites errors and omissions, which weakens the accuracy and legal standing of the record. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h6)
